subject.title: fix: carry reply metadata into runtime context

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this structured reply-ID payload as a trusted generic current-turn runtime contract now, and must alternate agent harnesses consume the same contract before it lands?
rationale: The patch is mechanically coherent, but repository evidence does not establish whether embedded-only delivery is an accepted permanent boundary or whether all supported harnesses must share this new trust and session-state contract.

options.title: Adopt cross-runtime contract
options.body: Approve the field allowlist and require parity or explicit unsupported-path coverage for alternate harnesses before merge.

options.title: Scope to embedded runtime
options.body: Approve the current implementation as intentionally embedded-only and track alternate-harness parity separately with clear tests and documentation.

options.title: Defer structured metadata
options.body: Keep the existing textual reply-context path until maintainers choose a broader channel-to-runtime contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt cross-runtime contract
recommendation.body: Approve the field allowlist and require parity or explicit unsupported-path coverage for alternate harnesses before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal is on the embedded prompt/runtime-context boundary where this contract is introduced.
